nodes.label: Structured Data Validation
nodes.rationale: Examples are starting points only; required properties must be verified against maintained Google Search and Schema.org documentation, and output is tested with the Rich Results Test and Schema.org Validator.

nodes.label: Agentic Browsing and AI Discoverability
nodes.rationale: Lighthouse Agentic Browsing signals, search indexing/ranking, and AI ingestion or citation are separate concerns; a browsable page or valid llms.txt does not prove an AI product will ingest, rank, or cite it.

nodes.label: Evidence-led Audit Workflow
nodes.rationale: A Lighthouse SEO score covers only a subset of technical checks and is not a ranking prediction, so findings are localized with live tools, fixed at the source, and re-verified; ranking outcomes remain pending search-engine validation.

nodes.label: llms.txt
nodes.rationale: llms.txt is an experimental proposal rather than a cross-vendor standard, so it is optional, never a ranking or citation factor, and never outranks crawlability, semantic HTML, and accurate metadata.

nodes.label: Structured Data (JSON-LD)
nodes.rationale: Schema markup must describe visible, accurate content and use the most specific applicable type; a type is never added solely to win a rich result, and syntax validity does not guarantee eligibility.

nodes.label: Title Tags
nodes.rationale: 50-60 characters is only a rough linting proxy; Google truncates title links to rendered width and may rewrite them from headings and anchor text, so accuracy matters more than automatic shortening.

nodes.label: Tailwind Best Practices
nodes.rationale: Utility composition is preferred over @apply for maintainability, mobile-first base styles are extended with responsive prefixes, and repeated patterns are extracted into components.

nodes.label: SSR Development (low-level)
nodes.rationale: Vite SSR is designed for meta-framework authors; app developers should use Nuxt/SvelteKit/Nitro instead.

nodes.label: CSS-First Configuration (@theme)
nodes.rationale: v4.1 eliminates JavaScript config files for most projects by defining design tokens directly in CSS.

nodes.label: Tailwind Utility-First Framework
nodes.rationale: Build-time scanning generates only used classes, yielding zero runtime overhead and no custom CSS naming.

nodes.label: Global Error Handler
nodes.rationale: Unexpected error details are logged but never leaked to clients in production; async handlers are wrapped so rejections reach the top-level middleware.

nodes.label: Layered Architecture
nodes.rationale: Controllers handle HTTP, services hold framework-agnostic business logic, and repositories own data access so layers can be mocked and the database swapped independently.

nodes.label: Validation Middleware
nodes.rationale: Validation happens at the request boundary with Zod schemas so invalid input fails fast before reaching business logic.

nodes.label: Node.js Architecture Principles
nodes.rationale: Layering yields testability, lets the database be replaced without touching business logic, and gives each layer a single responsibility.

nodes.label: Node.js Detailed Patterns and Worked Examples
nodes.norm_label: node.js detailed patterns and worked examples

nodes.label: PHP Pro MUST DO / MUST NOT DO Constraints
nodes.norm_label: php pro must do / must not do constraints
nodes.rationale: Delivery is blocked until PHPStan level 9 and the test suite pass clean, because strict types and static analysis catch defects that runtime testing alone misses.

nodes.label: artisan CLI entrypoint
nodes.rationale: Bootstraps Laravel via bootstrap/app.php and delegates console handling to handleCommand().

nodes.label: skills-lock.json skill registry

nodes.label: AI-generated design default traits to avoid
nodes.norm_label: ai-generated design default traits to avoid
nodes.rationale: Cream background plus serif display, acid-green-on-black, broadsheet rules, identical rounded SaaS cards, and template chrome appear regardless of subject, so they read as generated rather than chosen.

nodes.label: cPanel Git deployment procedure
nodes.rationale: The cPanel host has no SSH and cannot run Composer, so PHP dependencies are shipped as a pre-built vendor.zip and extracted over the existing vendor directory after each Git pull.

nodes.label: Laravel 11 to 12.71.0 security upgrade
nodes.rationale: Upgrade includes security fixes; main screens and authentication flows require post-deploy verification.

nodes.label: EnsureUtf8Response Middleware
nodes.rationale: Registered globally as a new middleware to guarantee UTF-8 encoded responses for every request.

nodes.label: Eloquent Performance Tips
nodes.rationale: Heavy work is pushed to queues rather than model events because model events execute synchronously inside the request cycle.

nodes.label: Query Optimization
nodes.rationale: Always eager load relationships to avoid N+1 queries; chunk or lazy-load large datasets to prevent memory exhaustion.

nodes.label: Job Patterns
nodes.rationale: Jobs are kept small, idempotent, and timeout-bounded so that retries are safe and workers cannot hang.

nodes.label: Repository Pattern
nodes.rationale: Data access sits behind an interface so the backing store can change and tests can substitute a mock implementation.

nodes.label: Service Layer Pattern
nodes.rationale: Business logic lives in a framework-injected service so controllers stay thin and the logic is independently testable.

nodes.label: PHPStan Configuration
nodes.rationale: PHPStan level 9 with strict and deprecation rules is enabled so type coverage is enforced statically rather than relying on runtime failures.

nodes.label: Container Queries (v4.1+)
nodes.rationale: Components respond to container size instead of viewport, enabling truly reusable responsive components.
